chunks: It cannot be said that He came into being after He had not been in existence, because in that case the attributes of the created things would be assigned to Him, and there would remain no difference between them and Him, and He would have no distinction over them. Thus, the Creator and the created would become equal and the initiator and the initiated would be on the same level. He created the creation without any example made by someone else, and He did not secure the assistance of any one out of His creation for creating it.

key_terms.الصِّفَاتُ الْمُحْدَثَاتُ: Attributes of the created things (temporal attributes)

ai.seo_question: How does Nahj al-Balagha define God's eternity and uniqueness in contrast to creation?
ai.summary: This passage articulates the Shia doctrine of divine simplicity by negating temporal origin (hadith al-jism) to prevent the attribution of changeable, created attributes to God, which would blur the ontological distinction between the Creator and the created. It emphasizes that God’s essence is free from composition and need, affirming that He brought existence into being from non-existence without any precedent or auxiliary assistance. This reinforces the concept of Tawhid al-Sifat, ensuring that God’s attributes are eternal and identical to His essence, unlike the contingent attributes of His creation.
